players.product: Power-secured HPC/AI data-center lease campuses (Lake Mariner NY for Fluidstack/Google; Justified & Muskie KY) - ex-Bitcoin-mining conversion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Patrick Fleury: first-quarter 2026 revenue was $34 million, down from $35.8 million in Q4 2025 on lower Bitcoin production, while HPC lease revenue increased to $21 million, up 117% from $9.7 million in Q4. CEO Paul Prager: this is the first period where HPC leasing is meaningfully reflected in the financials; digital asset revenue was about $13 million versus $21 million from HPC leasing, and revenue mix will keep shifting toward contracted HPC revenue as additional buildings come online in 2Q, 3Q and 4Q.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $34 million (vs $35.8 million in Q4); HPC lease revenue $21 million, up 117% from $9.7 million; digital asset revenue about $13 million

quarterly_data.signal: Lake Mariner status (CEO Prager / CTO Nazar Khan / CFO Fleury): 60 megawatts of critical IT capacity energized and generating revenue as of March 31; the second data hall in CB2 came online during the quarter, bringing all Core42 capacity into service (CB2 achieved ready for service in March and the Core42 lease commenced; all 60 critical MW delivered to Core42). For the Fluidstack deployment, CB3 is on track to complete TeraWulf's defined scope by the end of May, with Fluidstack and Google coordinating final energization and lease commencement; CB4 and CB5 remain on track for delivery in the third and fourth quarters of 2026, respectively. Construction for Fluidstack and Google incorporates customer-driven design refinements.
quarterly_data.figure: 60 megawatts of critical IT energized as of March 31; CB3 scope complete by the end of May; CB4 and CB5 delivery in the third and fourth quarters of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Kentucky (Hawesville / Justified) point-in-time status before the lease was signed: CEO Prager said TeraWulf expected to have a customer in place in the second quarter and was in late-stage negotiations after an extremely competitive process, and (asked whether a front runner existed) said 'we like somebody a lot for that site' and that he would assume it is going to be an investment grade, super high quality customer; the site offers immediate power availability and expansion potential with utility Big Rivers, and limited notice to proceed has been initiated. CFO Fleury: targeting 480 megawatts online in the second half of 2027; the $100 million bridge credit facility draw was repaid and the facility terminated after quarter end, and a portion of the approximately $1.2 billion of equity raised year to date will fund TeraWulf's equity contribution to the Kentucky project.
quarterly_data.figure: 480 megawatts online targeted in the second half of 2027; approximately $1.2 billion of equity raised year to date

quarterly_data.signal: HPC leasing segment profitability (CFO Fleury): as-reported quarterly segment profit margin was approximately 50% versus long-term guidance of approximately 85%, the gap driven by $2.1 million of tenant fit-out revenue and costs, $3.5 million of pre-revenue operating costs at WULF Compute, and $2.1 million of development costs across the 1.75 gigawatt portfolio of uncontracted development sites; adjusting for those yields approximately 85%. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was a negative $4.1 million, improved from negative $50.9 million in Q4; GAAP net loss of $427.6 million was driven mainly by non-cash fair value adjustments on the Google warrants ($216.3 million loss) and stock-based compensation. Demand response proceeds rose to $14.1 million from $4.4 million in Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: Segment profit margin approximately 50% reported / approximately 85% adjusted; adjusted EBITDA negative $4.1 million; 1.75 gigawatt uncontracted development portfolio

quarterly_data.signal: Liquidity and build spend as of March 31, 2026 (CFO Fleury): cash and restricted cash totaled $3.1 billion; the TeraWulf parent held approximately $300 million of unrestricted cash, increasing to approximately $1.5 billion including the equity raised in April. WULF Compute (Lake Mariner) remains on budget with approximately $2.8 billion of gross cash, $1.5 billion of CapEx spend complete and $2.2 billion remaining. The Abernathy JV had approximately $1.4 billion of gross cash, $0.4 billion of CapEx spend complete and $0.9 billion remaining. TeraWulf also closed a $250 million revolver from 8 different banks.
quarterly_data.figure: WULF Compute $1.5 billion of CapEx complete, $2.2 billion remaining; Abernathy JV $0.4 billion complete, $0.9 billion remaining; $250 million revolver

capex.period: remaining WULF Compute Lake Mariner build spend as of March 31, 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and power constraint (CEO Prager): the broader AI build-out is accelerating but increasingly constrained by power (interconnection delays, transmission limits, new generation) - 'The constraint is not GPUs, it is power.' Demand remains very strong with active engagement from hyperscalers and AI compute platforms; customers are pushing for prompt power and willing to contract for longer periods, and Prager does not see power supply coming online fast enough to meet demand. TeraWulf targets putting 250 to 500 MW in the ground in any given year. Pipeline items: Lake Mariner's incremental 250 MW interconnect awaits ISO feedback expected midyear; the Morgantown (Maryland) acquisition awaits a FERC decision expected mid-summer, with the existing 210 MW or so of peaker capacity to keep operating and battery storage plus gas-fired generation to be added incrementally.
quarterly_data.figure: 250 to 500 MW per year; incremental 250 MW Lake Mariner interconnect pending ISO feedback midyear; 210 MW existing Morgantown capacity

quarterly_data.signal: Lease terms and hardware evolution (CTO Khan): TeraWulf's initial contracts were 10 years (among the earlier contracts signed), while more recently the term has been 15 years, which has become well accepted in the market; with a tenant in place for 15 years, hardware changes will occur and contracts must align on how those transitions are handled. The design finalized with Fluidstack and Google toward the end of last year has gone through a couple of iterations as vendors evolve their hardware; TeraWulf works with AMD, NVIDIA and Google TPU hardware. Counterparty creditworthiness remains paramount, and CFO Fleury said the economic focus is NOI yield over cost to build aligned with the counterparty's credit support.
quarterly_data.figure: initial contracts 10 years; more recent market term 15 years

quarterly_data.signal: Mining wind-down and Abernathy (management): CFO Fleury said Bitcoin mining runs at somewhere between 5 and 6 exahash, will get no significant new investment, and TeraWulf will likely be out of that business by the next halving, with miners coming offline as buildings and power feeds are repositioned for HPC leasing; Q1 impairment included $8.9 million for shutting a mining facility to support HPC operations. CTO Khan said the Abernathy, Texas joint venture is being delivered under a lump-sum EPC agreement with Hypertec, with Fluidstack leading development and construction, and deployment sequencing and delivery timing are still being finalized with the ultimate compute end user.
quarterly_data.figure: 5-6 exahash mining range for the year

contracts.signal: CTO Nazar Khan: for the Fluidstack deployment at Lake Mariner (CB3, CB4 and CB5) all major project timelines remain unchanged; CB3 is on track to complete TeraWulf's defined scope by the end of May, with TeraWulf coordinating with Fluidstack and Google on final energization and lease commencement, and CB4 and CB5 remain on track for delivery in the third and fourth quarters of 2026, respectively.
